description: MANDATE-07 #7b NEGATIVE/BLIND-SPOT case: inject cartFailure=on via flagd and show the detector does NOT catch it. Kept in the labeled set on purpose. Measuring this set surfaced the reason: the .NET cart service exports no rpc_server_duration_milliseconds series at all — only http_server_request_duration_seconds for its own HTTP surface plus collector-generated traces_span_metrics_* — so grpc-error-rate-high, which is a ratio over rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count, has nothing to read for cart no matter how badly cart is failing. Nor does any other current rule cover it: the burn-rate rules key off http_server_request_duration_seconds 5xx, and cart's failures surface as gRPC status on the CALLER, not as 5xx on cart. This is an instrumentation gap, not a threshold that needs loosening, and tuning thresholds would not fix it. Expected verdict is FAIL until either cart emits server-side RPC metrics or a rule is added over traces_span_metrics_*. Recorded here so the gap stays visible instead of being quietly dropped from the set.
